entries.prompt: Create exactly ONE single full-body character sprite of the HI-TECH SOLDIER from the ORIGINAL METAL GEAR SOLID 2: SONS OF LIBERTY PS2 game. Use the attached original in-game model render and full-body reference faithfully for this exact MGS2 incarnation, not the Portable Ops Plus model. One figure, one still pose only, facing screen RIGHT in a readable three-quarter right combat-ready stance; boots planted naturally and completely visible. Detailed hand-painted 2.5D fighting-game sprite, restrained crisp contours and believable fabric/armor shading, high fidelity to the supplied game references rather than redesign. Match: matte black rounded helmet with its small side details and exposed warm amber/orange face-window area, very thick dark charcoal raised padded neck collar, large squared black shoulder armor, layered charcoal chest and belly armor, gray/olive/tan geometric camouflage sleeves and loose trousers, simple dark boots and gloves, brown-olive two-pouch waist equipment, dark central protective pelvis/groin panel. Keep the actual simple cloth-covered legs shown in the reference, not added futuristic knee armor. He holds the exact M4A1 carbine with M203 underbarrel grenade launcher shown in the reference, at controlled low-ready aimed diagonally toward screen right; realistic two-handed grip and plausible weapon length. Preserve actual gun parts, helmet profile, armor silhouette, camouflage colors and human proportions. Entire head, both boots, hands and rifle visible with a small clear margin all around. NO additional characters, alternate poses, panels, text, labels, UI, floor, cast shadow, vignette, smoke or glow. Background fully transparent RGBA, sharp solid figure silhouette without a surrounding halo. This is one original-costume static study for a game sprite catalog, not an animation sheet.

Create exactly ONE single full-body character sprite of the DIAMOND DOGS HELICOPTER PILOT "PEQUOD" model from METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN (1984). The attachments are original extracted TPP pilot models (standing T-pose and fixed seated variant) and an actual game cockpit closeup. Use only the standing pilot on the right of the first reference for the full body; the seated copy is a geometry comparison, not a second character to draw. Faithfully preserve this specific TPP model, not Morpho from Ground Zeroes and not the XOF jet pilot. One adult male pilot standing naturally and facing screen RIGHT in a readable three-quarter right side view, arms relaxed with one hand near his headset microphone as if checking a radio. Both feet fully visible and planted, no helicopter seat or vehicle. Detailed hand-painted 2.5D fighting-game sprite with restrained crisp contours, accurate materials and human anatomy, consistent quiet natural military palette. Exact clothing: sage/olive green zipped flight jacket, ribbed raised collar and ribbed dark cuffs/waistband, rectangular dark chest tabs, small upper-arm patch geometry as in the original model, olive flight trousers with the actual cargo pockets, muted olive gloves, plain dark low military pilot boots. A brown leather shoulder holster with holstered pistol sits low on the chest/ribcage on its diagonal dark crossbody strap, exactly as shown by the standing source, not a giant tactical vest. Helmet: off-white/light gray shell with olive central top/front visor housing, empty small black rectangular forehead mounting bracket, black side fasteners/communications fittings, green/dark chin strap and fine microphone boom ending beside the mouth. The actual visible face is clean-shaven with the narrow nose and serious adult expression in the cockpit reference. Keep visible helmet surfaces as documented; do not invent text or an unproven badge placement. No night-vision goggles, mask, extra rifle, body armor or modern redesign. Full figure from helmet to both boots with a small clear margin. NO second figure, reference grid, T-pose, captions, labels, UI, stage, floor, cast shadow, vignette, smoke or glow. Fully transparent RGBA background, clean solid edges and no halo. One static source pose, not animation frames. Record is a model-based interpretation pending tiny emblem/hidden geometry certification.
